system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review:** The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and efficiency note are not evidence of Buyer agreement. All positions remain subject to review. The recommendations below are negotiating proposals based on the supplied documents; the underlying DD documents and full SPA have not been provided.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate treatment for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 100% of price (AUD 24m)**, with any concession conditional on the overall protection package; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket, aggregation of related claims and exclusions for specially protected categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated; the Seller’s structure excludes both smaller systemic losses and the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General warranties: **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24–36 months** for general warranties, separate category-specific periods, and workable notification and proceedings requirements. | **Seek 36 months and reject blanket application**; 18 months may expire before issues emerge through full reporting and audit cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limits. | Separate protection for capacity, ownership, fully paid shares, absence of encumbrances and entitlement to transfer: no thresholds, substantially longer survival and at least purchase-price recourse. | **Require a separate regime, targeting a 100% price cap and at least six years’ survival**, subject to applicable law; Buyer must have meaningful recovery if it does not acquire the promised ownership. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions cover all Claims; no express fraud exception is supplied. | An express fraud/fraudulent-misrepresentation exception across caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure, knowledge, releases and remedy restrictions, covering relevant Seller-attributable conduct. | **Reject the package without a comprehensive fraud carve-out and preservation of non-excludable rights**; contractual protections must not shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced materials, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; specific warranty cross-references and an agreed, frozen disclosure bundle. | **Delete blanket deemed disclosure and require specific, fair disclosure**, accepting general disclosures only where narrowly agreed; document availability is not meaningful disclosure of every embedded risk. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Any Buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters merely discoverable from data-room or public records, bars claims. | Preferably no knowledge exclusion; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal-team members of the relevant facts and breach, without constructive or adviser-imputed knowledge. | **Delete “discoverable” and blanket adviser attribution; preserve indemnity and other agreed rights**; diligence access should not transfer unidentified Seller risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure confirms no final consent or evidence of satisfaction of associated conditions. | A Buyer-waivable CP requiring valid, effective consent under clauses 11.2–11.3, with all conditions satisfied and no unacceptable adverse changes. | **Require effective consent and evidence of condition satisfaction before Completion, with a long-stop termination right**; delivery of a conditional letter does not secure a customer contributing about 30% of revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release follows Completion. | Repayment and security discharge at Completion through binding bank payout/release arrangements; debt, interest and fees properly reflected in the equity-price bridge. | **Reject an unsecured promise of post-Completion release; require coordinated payout and effective releases at Completion**; the agreed debt-free/cash-free acquisition must not leave Buyer exposed to secured Seller-era debt. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses are characterised as Seller matters but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller-funded treatment through payment, retention or an express price deduction, including applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs; address later satisfaction of employment conditions. | **Itemise and allocate the full liability in the SPA and funds flow, without double counting**; contractual allocation alone does not fund a target-company payroll obligation inherited by Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, without independent payment verification, receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified settlement and effective IP vesting before Completion, plus a specific indemnity for losses arising from pre-Completion non-payment or defective ownership, including third-party claims and remediation costs. | **Require payment evidence and effective assignment/vesting documentation, backed by a broader indemnity outside general limitations**; paying an invoice alone may not establish ownership or cover resulting losses. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; possible export of approximately **1,240 records**, with access, scope and notification duties unresolved. | Prompt investigation, preservation/containment, legal assessment of notification obligations, Buyer oversight of material responses and targeted allocation of pre-Completion incident costs and liabilities. | **Keep open pending investigation and seek a specific indemnity and proportionate security if unresolved**; uncertainty is not evidence of immateriality, but neither does the record establish a confirmed notifiable breach. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, labelled ordinary-course costs. | Review them together for commitment dates, scope, necessity, termination rights, accruals and consistency with the price assumptions and conduct covenants. | **Do not accept the ordinary-course label without evidence; restrict new commitments and adjust price only where their proper classification warrants it**; related renewals may be material collectively, but future operating expenditure is not automatically debt-like. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Express, internally consistent regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, price adjustments, payment/completion covenants and fraud. | **Rewrite definitions and every operative limitation with explicit category exclusions and precedence rules**; a broad “all Claims” provision could silently defeat negotiated protections elsewhere. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s share register showing Harbourglass holds 100%. | Independent checks of issued capital, ownership chain, options/convertibles and other rights, encumbrances and transfer restrictions; appropriate corporate approvals and effective Completion transfers/register updates. | **Verify title rather than accept the register as conclusive, supported by fundamental warranties and releases**; a register alone does not establish unencumbered, transferable ownership of the entire equity. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties considered settled under the general regime. | A dedicated pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity with appropriate assessment-period survival and a separate cap; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement warranties with tailored survival/caps and Ironquay-specific protection. | **Expressly reserve both categories as open and negotiate distinct regimes**, including tax survival through relevant assessment periods plus a notification buffer; tax and core-IP exposure may emerge late and exceed the general warranty recovery. |

**Additional drafting guardrails:** Preserve claims notified within the applicable period until resolved, avoid short automatic litigation deadlines, and ensure disclosure of a known issue does **not** qualify the specific indemnity negotiated to cover it. Do not manufacture consent conditions: the supplied letter identifies an office-lease **notification** obligation and a Mossvale **assignment** restriction, neither of which presently establishes a share-sale consent requirement.
=== END ADVICE ===
